area: Local production for local consumption
label: Vision: Hawaii grows a growing share of the food it eats
text: Participants described a 2050 in which the import model is replaced by locally grown food, kupuna crops are abundant, food gardens and food forests are normal in community and home design, and disaster preparedness means strong local production capacity and supply chains rather than stockpiling. One pair set the marker at growing 50 percent of Hawaii's food locally by 2035.

area: Local production for local consumption
label: The state has a production goal with no baseline or recurring measure
text: Act 151 of 2019 directed a plan to double local food production by 2030 but set no baseline, unit or reporting requirement. The Census of Agriculture every five years is the closest proxy, and the Aloha+ dashboard shows the same 2022 sales figure as both production and consumption. The proportion of food produced and consumed locally, the 2050 Plan's indicator, has not been measured systematically since the state statistics bulletin ended in 2011.

area: Local production for local consumption
label: Affordability is the number one barrier to entering agriculture
text: Participants framed the constraint as cost of living: young people want to farm, but the cost of land, water and housing makes an agricultural livelihood hard to sustain, and farmworkers' quality of life is rarely counted. Wages, lease terms and the price of land were named alongside the price of food.
causal: When entering agriculture is unaffordable, fewer producers start or stay, so land stays fallow and production does not grow.

area: Local production for local consumption
label: Fallow state and county land is not moving into production
text: Participants expect rising food prices, SNAP reductions and food bank funding losses to raise demand for converting state and county land to food production, and asked the Agribusiness Development Corporation, the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Land and Natural Resources to plan how to get producers onto land quickly with irrigation and equipment.
causal: When public land stays fallow, the producers who could enter have nowhere to grow, which keeps production flat.
addresses: Affordability is the number one barrier to entering agriculture

area: Local production for local consumption
label: Production cannot be tracked in consistent units
text: No public series measures Act 151 production in dollars, pounds or acres year to year; the Census of Agriculture reports sales in dollars every five years, and the Cropland Data Layer gives acreage only from 2023. Without a series, growth cannot be distinguished from price inflation or from consolidation among a few large operations.
causal: When production cannot be measured, neither policy nor investment can be judged, and the goal stays rhetorical.
addresses: Fallow state and county land is not moving into production

area: Local production for local consumption
label: Institutional buyers are not yet a reliable market
text: State agencies required to buy local sit between 4 and 7 percent of food cost where the dollars are large; the Department of Education alone spends about $77 million a year on food. Producers cannot scale into a market that has not materialized.
causal: When institutional demand does not materialize, producers lack the contracts that would justify entering or expanding, which returns to affordability.
addresses: Production cannot be tracked in consistent units

area: Local production for local consumption
label: Build a recurring production measure paired with a farm-distribution measure
text: Assemble an annual production series from data that already exists (Cropland Data Layer acreage, state and USDA value series) and pair it with farm counts by sales and size class, so growth can be read as broad or concentrated. Develop it with the Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity's statistics staff.
addresses: Production cannot be tracked in consistent units;The state has a production goal with no baseline or recurring measure

area: Local production for local consumption
label: Move public land to producers with the supports they need
text: Convert fallow state and county land to food production with irrigation, equipment and long leases in place; participants proposed 99-year one-dollar regenerative leases with a focus on Native Hawaiian and ohana farms, transfer of 100,000 acres of public and ceded lands within five years, and taxing ag-zoned land held fallow or for speculation.
addresses: Fallow state and county land is not moving into production;Affordability is the number one barrier to entering agriculture
orgs: Agribusiness Development Corporation|Department of Land and Natural Resources

area: Local production for local consumption
label: Make farming a livable job
text: Participants proposed a universal basic income for regenerative food producers, housing vouchers for farmers as essential workers alongside teachers and health workers, and support for farmworkers' healthcare and housing.
addresses: Affordability is the number one barrier to entering agriculture

area: Local production for local consumption
label: GoFarm Hawaii beginning-farmer training and land access survey
text: GoFarm Hawaii trains beginning farmers across the islands and, with the statewide initiative, fielded a land access survey whose findings were forthcoming at the time of the convening.

area: Local production for local consumption
label: Nation of Hawaii, GoFarm and Purple Maia land-back-to-production cohort
text: A cohort run by Nation of Hawaii, GoFarm Hawaii and Purple Maia on turning land back into food production, including how to reduce barriers such as land cost and archaeological-site regulation where lineal descendants vote to restore traditional agriculture.

area: Local production for local consumption
label: Outcome: production measured annually and rising in volume, not only in price
text: A public series in consistent units, updated yearly, with farm counts by size so the room can see who benefits from growth.
addresses: Build a recurring production measure paired with a farm-distribution measure

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: Vision: public institutions anchor the local market
text: Participants want the purchasing power of schools, hospitals, prisons and hotels turned toward local producers: 60 percent local food in all schools by 2035 with annual benchmarks, five- to ten-year procurement contracts with producers, hotels sourcing 35 percent of ingredients locally by 2035, and a Local Food Transition Fund paid into by major importers and hotel chains.

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: Statutory purchasing data exists but is not consolidated or comparable
text: Acts 175 and 176 produce annual reports, but each agency files a separate PDF on its own basis (all food, produce only, food served, calendar or fiscal or school year) and no public source compiled them until this site did. The shares are not comparable across agencies.

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: The Department of Education has no centralized way to track local spending
text: The State Auditor's March 2026 report found handwritten ledgers, no centralized software, inconsistent definitions of local (mainland lettuce washed on Maui counted), and about $1 million a year of federal produce funds left unspent. The Department is at 6.5 percent against a 30 percent target for 2030.
causal: When the largest buyer cannot see its own local spending, it cannot manage toward the target, and suppliers get no reliable signal.

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: Local supply is not organized to meet institutional specifications
text: Agencies report that local sources of staple items are unavailable or cannot meet volume and specification; the Department of Corrections buys as much local produce as it can find but most of its $10 million goes to items not grown in Hawaii. Aggregation, processing and cold chain are thin: the Aloha+ dashboard counts nine produce processing and marshalling facilities statewide.
causal: When supply cannot meet institutional specifications, buyers default to imports, and the market signal to producers weakens further.
addresses: The Department of Education has no centralized way to track local spending

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: Rural commercial kitchens are priced out by wastewater rules
text: Maui County identified the Department of Health's wastewater calculation for commercial kitchens as a top barrier: projected use is overestimated for rural sites on septic, requiring impractically sized systems that community organizations cannot afford.
causal: When community kitchens cannot be built, value-added processing and meal programs stay small, which limits what institutions can buy locally.
addresses: Local supply is not organized to meet institutional specifications

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: Publish the compiled purchasing table with an owner and a common basis
text: Keep one public table of every agency's local share across years, name an owner for it, and get the five agencies to agree on one basis (all food purchased, a common definition of local, a stated year type). Publish it through the Hawaii Open Data portal.
addresses: Statutory purchasing data exists but is not consolidated or comparable

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: Track the flow of local produce into schools and other institutions
text: Participants asked for tracking of local produce into schools and institutions, with supplier identifiers and county of origin built into the Department of Education's purchasing software (an RFP was out at the convening) and the Act 185 food hub sales pilot.
addresses: The Department of Education has no centralized way to track local spending

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: Fix the wastewater formula for rural commercial kitchens
text: Alter the Department of Health's projected-use calculation for commercial kitchens in rural areas on septic so that community kitchens can be permitted at a realistic size.
addresses: Rural commercial kitchens are priced out by wastewater rules

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: Hawaii Good Food Alliance Regional Food Business Center
text: The Alliance leads planning, technical assistance and grants under the USDA Regional Food Business Center, the largest federal award to any organization in the set, aimed at the aggregation and business layer between farms and buyers.

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: Act 185 food hub sales pilot
text: A pilot that would produce the first public series of food hub sales disaggregable by producer and buyer; the Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity's report is due in 2027.

area: Institutional purchasing and the missing middle
label: Outcome: one table, one basis, and a market producers can plan around
text: Agencies report on the same basis, the table is maintained by a named owner, and multi-year contracts give producers a reason to scale.
addresses: Publish the compiled purchasing table with an owner and a common basis

area: Food access and household food security
label: Vision: everybody fed, and fed good food
text: Participants want food treated as a need to have, not a nice to have: a priority for families, communities and institutions, with the monetary barrier to buying local food reduced because people see its value for health and the economy.

area: Food access and household food security
label: Household food access has no statute, no target and no mandated measure
text: Hawaii recognizes no statutory right to food, sets no food-access target and requires no report. The only repeated local measure is the food banks' commissioned survey, which found 32 percent of households food insecure in 2024 to 2025 (30 percent in 2023), against a federal estimate near 10 percent. Continuity depends on the banks' fundraising.

area: Food access and household food security
label: Federal cuts are landing on the charitable network at once
text: Participants expect rising food prices, SNAP reductions and food bank funding losses together. The three food banks carry audited USDA food of about $11 million a year and Hawaii Foodbank alone reports $26 million in government grants; a cut at the top lands on partner agencies with one recorded source.
causal: When federal food and funding fall at the same time, the hubs that carry most partner agencies have less to pass on, and single-source agencies have no recorded alternative.

area: Food access and household food security
label: Neighbor islands carry the highest need with the thinnest recorded network
text: Hawaii and Maui counties have food insecurity around 40 percent of households and the highest ALICE shares, yet nearly all recorded organizational grant flow lands on Oahu, and the neighbor-island food banks itemize few organizational grantees on their filings.
causal: When the recorded network is thinnest where need is highest, coordination cannot see where support is missing or how inter-island supply actually works.
addresses: Federal cuts are landing on the charitable network at once

area: Food access and household food security
label: Demand-side and supply-side data cannot be read together
text: Food-access stewards (the food banks, Aloha United Way's 211 and ALICE, the Hawaii Data Collaborative) and production stewards share no common identifiers or joint reporting, so the two sides of the same system are read in separate reports.
causal: When supply and demand data cannot be joined, a purchasing gain or a production loss cannot be traced to households, and the food-security goal stays unmeasured.
addresses: Neighbor islands carry the highest need with the thinnest recorded network

area: Food access and household food security
label: Fund the food banks' statewide survey publicly and name an owner
text: Recurring public funding for the household food security survey, with county tables published as data, so the state measures the outcome its own strategy names.
addresses: Household food access has no statute, no target and no mandated measure
orgs: Hawaii Foodbank|Maui Food Bank|The Food Basket

area: Food access and household food security
label: Connect food access indicators to the production and purchasing numbers
text: Track a food-access indicator with the Hawaii Data Collaborative and Hawaii Foodbank alongside production and purchasing, using shared identifiers, so both sides of the system can be read together.
addresses: Demand-side and supply-side data cannot be read together

area: Food access and household food security
label: Weave a five-year food plan into the Medicaid 1115 waiver
text: One pair proposed carrying a five-year food plan into the state's Medicaid 1115 waiver, linking food access to health financing.
addresses: Household food access has no statute, no target and no mandated measure

area: Food access and household food security
label: The State of Food Insecurity in Hawaii survey
text: Commissioned by the four food banks, fielded on the USDA household module with county quotas and weighted to the American Community Survey; two waves so far (2023 and 2024 to 2025). The only repeated, county-resolved measure of any food goal.
orgs: Hawaii Foodbank|Maui Food Bank|The Food Basket

area: Food access and household food security
label: Neighbor Connector intake at food distributions
text: Hawaii Foodbank's paperless check-in (Feeding America's Service Insights) records age, ethnicity and household size at the point of service, an administrative complement to the survey that can describe small places.

area: Food access and household food security
label: Maui County quarterly food security tracking with Maui Food Bank
text: The county's Department of Agriculture tracks quarterly food security trends with Maui Food Bank and publishes annual updates on its Food and Nutrition Security Plan metrics.
orgs: Maui County Department of Agriculture|Maui Food Bank

area: Food access and household food security
label: Outcome: a food-access measure with an owner, read beside supply
text: A recurring, publicly funded household measure by county, joined to production and purchasing by shared identifiers.
addresses: Fund the food banks' statewide survey publicly and name an owner

area: Culturally relevant food and food as medicine
label: Culturally relevant food and health outcomes are tracked program by program
text: Food is Medicine programs track clinical outcomes (A1c, BMI, blood pressure, medication use, food insecurity screening, healthcare utilization and cultural relevancy of care), but the data live in separate program systems and are not yet a statewide series.

area: Culturally relevant food and food as medicine
label: Build a monitoring, evaluation and learning model across Food is Medicine programs
text: The Hawaii Good Food Alliance is developing a monitoring, evaluation and learning model through its Food is Medicine work; participants asked that the clinical and cultural-relevancy indicators be designed for interoperability with CRMs and Airtable from the start.
addresses: Culturally relevant food and health outcomes are tracked program by program

area: Culturally relevant food and food as medicine
label: Hawaii Good Food Alliance Food is Medicine programs
text: Programs that pair produce and culturally relevant food with health care, with participation data collected by the Alliance and partners.

area: Culturally relevant food and food as medicine
label: GusNIP produce prescription awards in Hawaii
text: USDA produce prescription awards to Hawaii recipients total about $20 million since 2020 in the federal award record, the fourth-largest food program reaching nonprofits here.

area: Aina restoration and ecosystem health
label: Practice and ecosystem indicators are collected site by site
text: Participants listed the indicators they would track (cover cropping, drip irrigation, no-spray and no-till practice, soil carbon, biodiversity) and noted graduate students working on soil abundance visualization; the data are gathered by sensors and assessments at partner sites, not as a statewide series.

area: Aina restoration and ecosystem health
label: Compare environmental and agricultural data across sites
text: Purple Maia plans to compare ecosystem and agricultural data across partner sites, with narratives generated for site managers; a statewide roll-up would need shared units and consent from the organizations whose sites are measured.
addresses: Practice and ecosystem indicators are collected site by site

area: Aina restoration and ecosystem health
label: KILO Dashboard
text: Purple Maia's dashboard aggregates water, soil and air sensor data across partner sites into per-site health gauges with generated narratives and a chatbot; partner access now, public access under consideration.

area: Land justice and land back
label: Land under Indigenous stewardship is not inventoried
text: Participants asked for an inventory of lands meaningfully under Indigenous stewardship and for programming that turns land back into food production, including reducing land cost and resolving archaeological-site rules where lineal descendants choose to restore traditional agriculture. No public series exists.

area: Land justice and land back
label: Long, cheap, regenerative leases for local and Native Hawaiian producers
text: Participants proposed 99-year one-dollar regenerative leases with a focus on Native Hawaiian farmers and ohana-based farming, transfer of 100,000 acres of public and ceded lands to cooperatives and subsistence farms within five years, and a prohibition on large leaseholds to multinational agribusiness.
addresses: Land under Indigenous stewardship is not inventoried

area: Land justice and land back
label: Track lease length and tenure alongside production
text: Average lease length for farms and ranches, and producer tenure (lessee or owner, renter or homeowner), were on the convening's metric wishlist; they sit in Agribusiness Development Corporation, Department of Land and Natural Resources and Department of Hawaiian Home Lands records with no public series.
addresses: Land under Indigenous stewardship is not inventoried

area: Land justice and land back
label: Hawaiian home lands reference layer on this site
text: The Department of Hawaiian Home Lands' official inventory is drawn on the map as an outline for orientation; no figure on this site is computed by home-land status.

area: Climate resilience and disaster-ready food systems
label: Disaster readiness is understood as production capacity, not stockpiles
text: Participants framed resilience as strong local production and supply chains rather than stockpiling, and pointed to the Maui wildfires: the ALICE share in Maui County rose nine points after August 2023, and Maui's food insecurity estimate sits around 40 percent.

area: Climate resilience and disaster-ready food systems
label: Read supply shocks through the network
text: Use the recorded network to see which hubs carry federal food and money, which agencies depend on one source, and how inter-island supply moves, so a shock can be traced before it lands. This site's Food security tab is a first version.
addresses: Disaster readiness is understood as production capacity, not stockpiles

area: Climate resilience and disaster-ready food systems
label: Food bank Maui wildfire response
text: Hawaii Foodbank's Maui wildfires response and recovery report documents the charitable network's role after August 2023.

area: Water access, equity and management
label: Water access for Hawaiian home lands lessees needs statewide coordination
text: Participants asked how statewide coordination could work between agencies, including the Agribusiness Development Corporation, the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Hawaiian Home Lands, to protect water access for lessees on Maui and lower water rates for Molokai lessees.

area: Water access, equity and management
label: Coordinate water access across state agencies and counties
text: Work through individual counties and the state agencies that hold water and land to secure access and affordable rates for producers, with lessees on Hawaiian home lands first.
addresses: Water access for Hawaiian home lands lessees needs statewide coordination

area: Food waste reduction and circular economy
label: Circular-economy output is not measured
text: Participants asked to track the production output of local waste-reduction and circular-economy companies such as Hawaiian Earth and Aloha Harvest, including in-state fertilizer and feed producers.

area: Food waste reduction and circular economy
label: Aloha Harvest food rescue
text: Aloha Harvest rescues and redistributes food on Oahu; it is the second-largest distributor in the recorded network, giving out about $13 million of food in its latest filing.

area: Food waste reduction and circular economy
label: Track diverted food and compost output as a series
text: Report pounds rescued, composted and returned to soil by the organizations doing it, so the circular economy has a number the room can watch.
addresses: Circular-economy output is not measured

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Vision: a coordination framework that tracks progress and tells the truth about capacity
text: By 2030 participants want a statewide food systems coordination framework with ways to track progress, real policy and on-the-ground results, transparency and information sharing, trust among partners, and the honesty to say when a need is not met and then make policy to meet it.

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Nine data stewards, no owner for the whole picture
text: Government stewards publish statistics but largely repackage federal series; the university builds standards but hosts no series; nonprofits run the flagship tracker and the only repeated survey; private consultancies fill gaps under contract. No steward type owns the whole picture, which is why a coordination initiative has a role.

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Prospective dashboards outnumber live ones
text: Several of the most-cited efforts (Maui County's dashboard and access map, Purple Maia's public access, Hawaii Investment Ready's framework) were in development at the time of the assessment; definitions, disaggregations, periods and platforms differ.
causal: When systems are built separately, definitions harden before they are shared, and joining them later becomes expensive.

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Metrics are listed as tracked with no one responsible
text: Guam's dashboard gives every metric an action lead, partners and a status; Aloha+ has status flags but no owners. In Hawaii nothing is tracked in a way that names who keeps it current.
causal: When no one owns a metric, it lapses, as the percent-local series did in 2011.
addresses: Prospective dashboards outnumber live ones

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Communications, analysis and evaluation capacity are thin and uncoordinated
text: The coordination team's own agenda asks how to analyze new information quickly for specialist and public audiences, whether professional messaging is needed, how to boost visibility of results, and how to work with evaluators and philanthropic partners consistently.
causal: When results are not analyzed and communicated, decision makers do not act on them, and the case for owners and funding is never made.
addresses: Metrics are listed as tracked with no one responsible

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Assign an owner, partners and a status to every key metric
text: Adopt Guam's accountability scaffold: a lead, named partners and a current status for each metric, so nothing is listed as tracked with no one responsible.
addresses: Metrics are listed as tracked with no one responsible

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Agree shared definitions and identifiers while systems are still forming
text: Start with a small set of shared metrics, stable identifiers for the units data is sliced by (island, county, moku, organization), and agreed exchange formats; publish through the Hawaii Open Data portal rather than a new platform.
addresses: Prospective dashboards outnumber live ones

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Keep a living inventory of who is doing what
text: Maintain the steward activity matrix as a living resource rather than a one-time snapshot, identify missing organizations and programs, and keep sharing data; this site's steward inventory is seeded from the convening's matrix.
addresses: Nine data stewards, no owner for the whole picture

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Build metrics into Aloha+ before standing up anything new
text: Strengthen the Aloha+ Challenge local-food goal area with better production and consumption numbers and a named maintainer, and decide deliberately whether a standalone site is worth building.
addresses: Prospective dashboards outnumber live ones

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Food+ Bill Tracker and policy incubator
text: Purple Maia's Hawaii Food+ Policy team has tracked food-system bills since 2021 and publishes a live tracker for the 2026 session grouped by legislative stage and tagged by topic, with lists of bills needing testimony and bills at risk of dying, alongside a summer policy incubator.

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Aloha+ Challenge Dashboard
text: The state's goals platform, government-housed on an open-data platform and jointly led by the State, the four counties and the Office of Hawaiian Affairs, with a local food production and consumption goal area and per-indicator status flags.

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Food System Sustainability Indicator and Metric System
text: UH West Oahu's Ke O Mau Center and Transforming Hawaii's Food System Together are building an indicator system aligned to the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals, piloted through a published Delphi ranking of food-security indicators for Hawaii, to feed the Aloha+ dashboard.
orgs: UH West Oahu Ke O Mau Center|Transforming Hawaii's Food System Together

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Statewide Food Systems Coordination monthly call and working group
text: Oahu RC&D convenes a monthly coordination call, a state food systems working group page, the data landscape convenings, and a data call on 2026 requests.
orgs: Oahu Resource Conservation and Development Council

area: Institutional capacity and policy reform
label: Outcome: shared infrastructure that lets existing stewards work together
text: Clear ownership for each metric, a living inventory, shared definitions and identifiers, and coordination capacity that turns fragmented datasets into a shared picture of progress.
addresses: Assign an owner, partners and a status to every key metric

area: Food systems investment and business performance
label: Capital for the food system was mapped once
text: Hawaii Investment Ready's 2022 Capital Scan mapped who funds what; a systemic investing framework is in development and intended to be public. Foundation and intermediary grants to food organizations appear annually in public filings and could refresh the picture every year.

area: Food systems investment and business performance
label: Refresh the capital picture annually from public filings
text: Use Form 990 Schedule I and 990-PF grant rows, federal awards and audits, as this site does, to update who funds food-system work each year, and add investment data the framework collects.
addresses: Capital for the food system was mapped once

area: Food systems investment and business performance
label: Hawaii Investment Ready food systems investing framework
text: Research, data collection, stakeholder engagement and systems mapping to move capital more strategically for systems change; to be a public resource when complete.

area: Food systems investment and business performance
label: Farm profitability analysis
text: The Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity's 2025 profitability analysis found profitability concentrated in narrow sales and acreage categories, which motivates tracking farm distribution by size alongside production totals.
